title: Myanmar Open Wordnet: v0.1.2 romanised variants and v0.1.3 release
author: Wenjie Wang; Francis Bond
scope: MOW project page states v0.1.2 includes romanised and ASCII-friendly variants for searching via both MLCTS and MLCTS 2 (the latter used in the MLC Myanmar-English Dictionary), plus Simple and Simple2; v0.1.3 downloadable release contains synset-lemma pairs and is CC BY 4.0. This is a secondary lexical resource and system-use statement, not the MLC primary specification or proof that every variant is correct.

title: Language policy and language planning in Burma
author: Anna J. Allott
scope: Pacific Linguistics Series A No.67, pp.131-154. The chapter reports that the MLC Concise Burmese Dictionary was issued in five parts from late 1978 through 1980, established official orthography and supplied pronunciations. Secondary historical description only; it does not reproduce the dictionary, transcription notation or MLCTS table. Online edition licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

title: Review of Denise Bernot: Dictionnaire birman-français
author: John Okell
scope: Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 6(2), pp.89-104. Bibliography identifies the MLC concise dictionary as a five-volume 1978-1980 work, Rangoon, Mranmācā Aphwai. Bibliographic lead only; the review does not inspect its pronunciation key or MLCTS table.

title: Myanmar Open Wordnet (MOW) v0.1.3 Burmese lemma release
author: Myanmar Open Wordnet project
scope: Official MOW repository release file mow-0.1.3-mya_20171005165336.tab; file header identifies MOW 0.1.3, language mya and CC BY 4.0. README states the repository hosts release TSV files and that the wordnet is CC BY 4.0. This release contains orthographic Burmese lemma rows; it does not provide pronunciations or establish syllable segmentation for the present suffix-matching audit. Upstream Git blob SHA 0c97fc4e98b3827dae0bc667858993037496ca58.

title: Sealang Burmese Shortcut: third-party API request implementation
author: vpnry
scope: Third-party open-source wrapper constructs dictionary requests as http://sealang.net/api/api.pl?service=dictionary&lang=burmese&query=<word> (and query=text for Google mode). This is implementation evidence for the historical request URL/parameter spelling only; it does not establish the current API response schema or dictionary entry field semantics.

title: Myanmar (Burmese) Orthography Notes
author: Richard Ishida
scope: Descriptive secondary synthesis, updated 2026-04-28. Section Additional phonetic details > Rhymes tabulates vowel/final/tone combinations in IPA and explicitly states that the table does not account for vowel reduction. Uses N as a placeless nasal archiphoneme for coda values. The phonology inventory section cites Wikipedia as a source; this is not an MLC primary transcription table and should not be treated as an independent primary source.

title: Proposal of 4 Myanmar semivowels
author: Myanmar Unicode and NLP Research Center
scope: National contribution to ISO/IEC JTC1/SC2/WG2 N2827, dated 2004-06-21. It identifies the MLC Myanmar Orthography published October 1986 as the Ministry-prescribed national standard and describes four basic medials plus combinations totalling eleven symbols. This is a Unicode proposal citing the MLC standard, not the MLC book itself and not an MLCTS/phonological transcription table.

title: မြန်မာစာလုံးပေါင်းသတ်ပုံကျမ်း (MLC Burmese spelling/orthography treatise)
author: မြန်မာစာအဖွဲ့ (Myanmar Language Commission)
scope: National Library of Myanmar E-Resources bibliographic record 189: MLC publisher, Yangon, 1986; second edition; 292 pages; 23 cm; PDF option listed. This appears to correspond to the October 1986 MLC orthography standard cited by Unicode WG2 N2827; identity with the separate partial scan titled Myanmar Spelling Dictionary in Unicode L2/10-360 is not confirmed. The book contents were not inspected: the E-Resources record itself returned 502 during retrieval. Do not infer any pronunciation key or MLCTS/IPA table from this catalog record.

title: Myanmar Spelling Dictionary (partial scanned pages and character pronunciation list)
author: Union of Myanmar Education Ministry, Myanmar Department
scope: Unicode WG2 document L2/10-360 reproduces a scan labelled Myanmar Spelling Dictionary, published 1986. Page 1 includes a Characters pronunciation List and an image of original page 1; pages 2-9 show additional original spelling pages. The document's explanatory note says the character pronunciation list corresponds to a Myanmar Language Character Map and discusses sorting. This is a partial scan, not a complete book or an MLCTS/IPA rime table; its identity relative to the MLC Myanmar Orthography title in N2827/National Library record 189 needs confirmation.

title: မြန်မာစာလုံးပေါင်းသတ်ပုံကျမ်း (National Diet Library catalogue record)
author: Burma. Paññā reʺ Vanʿ krīʺ Ṭhāna. Mranʿ mā Cā ʾA phvaiʹ
scope: National Diet Library of Japan record R100000136-I1970023484907173422: Burmese-language orthography/spelling reference published by the Ministry of Education Myanmar Language Commission in 1978; physical book, 17 cm; NDC 829.351; catalogue summary identifies Burmese orthography and spelling. Bibliographic access lead only; no pages, pronunciation key, MLCTS table or lexical entries inspected. Allott (1985, p.145) separately reports a MLC spelling book published in 1978 and a five-part Concise Burmese Dictionary issued from late 1978 to 1980; exact title identity and relationship require title-page verification.

title: မြန်မာစာလုံးပေါင်းသတ်ပုံကျမ်း (CiNii Books holdings record)
author: National Institute of Informatics; CiNii Books
scope: CiNii Books record NCID BA69415754 confirms the 1978 MLC publication and provides fuller physical description: 28, 379 pages, 17 cm; three Japanese library holdings (Osaka University and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies locations). Google Books record identifies the original as University of Michigan and a digitized 379-page 2007 scan, but only snippet-view metadata is exposed in the search result. These are access/identity leads, not inspected page content or evidence of pronunciation/MLCTS/IPA fields.

title: Myanmar-English dictionary (1996 reprint; Google Books digitization record)
author: Myanmar Language Commission; Dunwoody Press; Google Books
scope: Google Books bibliographic record identifies the 1996 Dunwoody Press reprint of the MLC 1993 Myanmar-English Dictionary; original from the University of Michigan; digitized 2008-05-15; 635 pages. Bibliographic/digitization metadata only: no page-level dictionary entries, transcription key or MLC table were inspected in this review.

title: Burmese Dictionary / SEAlang Library Burmese Dictionary metadata
author: SHACHI Language Resource Metadata Database; SEAlang Library
scope: Independent resource metadata describes a ~35,000-entry Burmese lexicon sourced from the MLC 1993 Myanmar-English Dictionary (1996 Dunwoody Press reprint), states the interface supports IPA phonetic search/display, and identifies source-material copyright as MLC 1993 / Dunwoody 1996. Metadata only: no entry records, internal field schema, MLCTS2 column or reusable dictionary data inspected.

title: Myanmar Text-To-Speech System with Rule-based Tone Synthesis
author: Kyawt Yin Win; Tomio Takara
scope: Four formal Standard Myanmar tone categories: level, falling/creaky, high-falling/high, and extremely short checked with glottal stop. Models average syllable-center F0 and syllable duration; reports 180 CV words across five speakers (two Yangon natives, one lower Myanmar, one upper Myanmar). Table examples on /la/ include လ /là/ moon, လာ /la/ come, လား /lá/ dray horse, လတ် /laʔ/ fresh. These are tone illustrations, not a formally controlled minimal-pair set and not evidence for the eight MLCTS rime collisions.

title: myMediCon: End-to-End Burmese Automatic Speech Recognition for Medical Conversations
author: Hay Man Htun; Ye Kyaw Thu; H. Chanlekha; Kotaro Funakoshi; Thepchai Supnithi
scope: Reports orthographic ASR reference transcripts and word/syllable segmentation, not IPA or phonemic pronunciation labels. Authors say they plan future corpus release; no corpus download URL or corpus license is specified in the paper. The paper CC BY-NC 4.0 notice applies to the paper, not automatically to the corpus. Not an IPA gold or lexical pronunciation resource.
